trust_decision.summary: The upgrade listener decides whether a per-request waiter (holding the IncomingMessage and a never-settling Promise) is removed from the shared waiterMap; at the pinned commit it is only removed on a successful 'connection' or on the reject branch, so a handshake that ws aborts after the waiter was set keeps it forever.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'aborted WebSocket handshake'; the only handshake call is wss.handleUpgrade inside setupWebSocket, next to the waiterMap.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All five sites are in src/websocket.ts; the upgradeWebSocket consumer (src/websocket.ts:252-268) is the same file and module as the landing point.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the uncovered routes: the fetchCallback-throws branch (src/websocket.ts:214-218) looks like an app error path already answered with 500, and the client-disconnect-during-fetch race looks like a ws/Node lifecycle concern rather than the 'aborted handshake' the report names.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A successful upgrade must still resolve the waiter and fire onOpen/messages; also other server 'upgrade' listeners (listenerCount > 1) must not have their sockets ended, and messages buffered during onOpen must still be delivered. An over-broad fix (e.g. deleting the waiter before handleUpgrade, or rejecting on any socket close including after upgrade) breaks open or close semantics.

O6_input_shapes: upgrade rejected by app (non-matching or missing waiter symbol) -> waiter rejected (fix.diff:47)
handshake aborted by ws after waiter matched (invalid Sec-WebSocket-Key in the test; any ws abortHandshake that destroys the socket) -> reclaimed on socket 'close' (fix.diff:57-58)

O7_producer.where: The leaked state is produced by waitForWebSocket (src/websocket.ts:185-189) via upgradeWebSocket (src/websocket.ts:268), in the same file as the check; no schema/serializer/cache.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: fetchCallback throws after upgradeWebSocket already registered a waiter (e.g. a later middleware or user fetch wrapper throws); catch branch returns without deleting/rejecting the waiter, and the fix did not touch it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks like a generic app-error path that already sends 500; Hono's app.fetch usually converts errors via onError, so only custom fetch wrappers or a rethrowing onError reach it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~10 lines above the fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: client socket closes while fetchCallback is still awaiting (slow auth middleware); the fix's socket.once('close') is registered only after the await, so a close that already fired never reclaims the waiter if ws then silently destroys the non-readable socket.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Race on client disconnect looks like a ws/Node lifecycle concern, not the 'aborted handshake' the report describes; reproducing it needs a timed disconnect.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; depends on ws completeUpgrade behaviour outside the repo

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Already a natural sibling: the error branch returning early without reclaiming the waiter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer writing the error branch thinks only of answering 500, not of state registered by the middleware that ran before the throw.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second upgrade path (e.g. an h2/secure server or a manual handleUpgrade helper for users with listenerCount > 1) that reuses waitForWebSocket but not rejectWaiter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The adapter already supports a custom createServer (src/server.ts:16) and co-existing upgrade listeners (src/websocket.ts:215,225); a second helper sharing the waiter map is a plausible addition.

O9_family: CWE-401/CWE-770 missing release of per-request state (memory leak) on aborted WebSocket handshake

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=20, pnpm 11, vitest 4, tsdown; dev dep ws ^8.19 and hono ^4.12 (package.json:93-116)
O10_build.project_tests: test/websocket.test.ts (connect, reject, header forwarding, other upgrade listeners); the fix test uses FinalizationRegistry plus global.gc, so it needs node --expose-gc for a reliable signal (fix.diff:97-149)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the waiter in a finally after wss.handleUpgrade, or add a socket 'close' listener only around handleUpgrade, leaving the fetchCallback-throw branch and the pre-await disconnect open and the pending promise in upgradeWebSocket unsettled.

out_of_scope_notes: When a waiter matches, the listener calls handleUpgrade regardless of the app's response status (src/websocket.ts:221-241), so a later middleware returning 401 does not block the upgrade; this is an access-control question, not this leak.
